userStories.title: GitHub HTTP client, errors and rate limits
userStories.description: As a developer I need one robust client for GitHub GraphQL and REST so failures are classified consistently.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/github/client.ts: createGitHubClient({ token, apiUrl, fetch? }) with graphql<T>(query, variables) and rest<T>(method, path, body?)
Sends Authorization: Bearer, Accept, X-GitHub-Api-Version (REST); 20 s timeout via AbortSignal

GitHubError with kind (ErrorKind in model.ts), status, message, resetAt, retryAfterSeconds; GraphQL `errors` arrays map to graphql/not_found/forbidden kinds; 401 -> unauthorized; 403/429 with x-ratelimit-remaining: 0 or retry-after -> rate_limited; secondary rate limits handled; 5xx -> server; fetch failure/abort -> network
parseRateLimit from headers and from the GraphQL rateLimit object
The token never appears in error messages, causes or toString() output (tested)
Coverage >= 95% for src/lib/github
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)
userStories.notes: client.ts (graphql with opt-in partial, rest), errors.ts (GitHubError, status and GraphQL type classification), rateLimit.ts (parseRateLimit); 100% coverage; no cause on network errors, token masked in server messages; restResponse (headers, e.g. x-oauth-scopes) is left to US-011.

userStories.title: Diff engine: detect what changed between polls
userStories.description: As a user I want to be told exactly what changed: CI failed, CI passed after failure, new review, approved, changes requested, new comment, ready to merge, merged/closed by someone else.
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/diff/diffSnapshots.ts: diffSnapshots(prev | null, next, viewerLogin) -> PrEvent[] (types in model.ts); prev null -> []
ci_failed on transition to failure (also after a new head commit); ci_passed only when the previous state was failure
review_new/approved/changes_requested per new review id by someone other than the viewer
comment_new when commentCount increases and the last comment author is not the viewer
ready_to_merge on transition into ready (not draft, mergeStateStatus clean, or approved/no review required + checks success/none + mergeable)
merged/closed only when the actor is not the viewer; PRs that simply left the search scope produce nothing
Event ids are deterministic (dedupe across repeated polls); events sorted by time
Table-driven unit tests; coverage >= 95% for src/lib/diff
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)
userStories.notes: diffSnapshots + isReadyToMerge in src/lib/diff (100% coverage, 51 table-driven tests); ci_passed is literal (previous poll failure), so failure -> pending -> success needs the poller to pass the last settled check state (docs/architecture.md Diff engine).

userStories.title: Background poller with alarms, backoff and rate-limit awareness
userStories.description: As a user I want Prowl to stay up to date in the background without burning my GitHub rate limit.
acceptanceCriteria: src/background/poller.ts: schedules alarm `poll` every settings.pollIntervalMinutes (min 1, default 2); reschedules when settings change; runs on install/startup when signed in
Single-flight: concurrent triggers share one in-flight poll
Exponential backoff with jitter on errors (interval x 2^n, max 30 min); rate_limited or remaining < 100 waits until resetAt; unauthorized stops polling and surfaces the error
Persists snapshot + pollState (model.ts) and prunes local state for PRs that no longer exist
src/background/messages.ts routes BackgroundRequest messages ({type:'poll', force}, markSeen, signedOut)
src/lib/time/backoff.ts pure + tested; poller unit tests use fake timers and the chrome fake
E2E: with auth seeded through the service worker, a forced poll fetches from the mock and stores a snapshot; tests/e2e/fixtures.ts gains signIn() and poll() helpers
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)
userStories.notes: poller.ts (alarm, single-flight, backoff/rate-limit waits via src/lib/time/backoff.ts, sign-out-safe writes, prune), messages.ts (poll/markSeen/signedOut), Snapshot.sectionErrors + settledChecks (ci_passed across pending); hook for US-008/009 is the end of runPoll; E2E fixtures signIn()/poll(), tests/e2e/poller.spec.ts.

userStories.title: Context7 audit of platform and library APIs, minor/patch updates
userStories.description: As a maintainer I want Prowl on current, non-deprecated APIs and the latest compatible versions of its dependencies.
acceptanceCriteria: Load the Context7 tools (ToolSearch `select:mcp__Context7__resolve-library-id,mcp__Context7__query-docs`) and check every API Prowl uses against current docs: chrome.sidePanel, alarms, notifications, permissions, storage, action, runtime messaging and the MV3 manifest keys; Preact 10 + @preact/signals; Vite 8 (rolldownOptions); Vitest 5; Playwright; Astro; Biome 2. Fix each deprecated or outdated usage found

Apply minor and patch updates within the current majors (`pnpm update`, lockfile regenerated by pnpm); Biome may move to its newest 2.x with `biome migrate`; Playwright stays pinned at 1.56.1 (sandbox Chromium); no major bump (TypeScript 6, Preact 10, Vite 8, Vitest 5 stay)
One line in docs/decisions.md per deliberate non-upgrade or API choice the audit confirmed; the audit results (checked, changed, left) summarized in the progress.txt entry
Perf budget still holds (`pnpm size`)
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)
userStories.notes: Chrome and Preact checked with Context7 (quota then ended; the rest via installed types, a deprecation scan and build output); 12 deprecated Preact type uses fixed; lockfile refreshed; decisions recorded.

userStories.title: Crisp screenshots at 2x device pixel ratio
userStories.description: As a visitor of the README, the site or the Chrome Web Store listing I want sharp screenshots on HiDPI screens.
acceptanceCriteria: `pnpm screenshots` writes every docs/screenshots/*.png at device scale factor 2 (a 400 x 760 panel becomes 800 x 1520 px); routine E2E runs keep their current speed (2x only where a screenshot is written, or proven not to slow the suite)

README, docs and the site display them at their CSS size (400 px wide: width/height attributes or styles), so layouts do not change; the site's Lighthouse gate stays >= 95 in every category (resize/compress or srcset as needed)

`scripts/store-images.mjs` uses the 2x sources and still outputs exactly 1280 x 800, 440 x 280 and 1400 x 560 PNGs; docs/screenshots and docs/store regenerated and opened with the Read tool to confirm they are sharp
Codebase patterns in progress.txt updated (how screenshots are captured)
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)
userStories.notes: Screenshots captured at 2x (800 x 1520) via context deviceScaleFactor only under PROWL_SCREENSHOTS=1; settings.png routed through saveScreenshot; README/docs/site show 400 x 760 CSS px (srcset 1x/2x); store images regenerated at exact sizes; Lighthouse 100 everywhere.

userStories.title: Guarantee Prowl never reads site content
userStories.description: As a user I want proof that Prowl cannot read or change the pages I visit.
acceptanceCriteria: A manifest test fails the build if the production manifest gains anything that can touch pages: `permissions` must equal exactly sidePanel, storage, alarms, notifications; `host_permissions` exactly https://api.github.com/*; `optional_host_permissions` exactly https://github.com/* (device flow); no `content_scripts`, `web_accessible_resources`, `externally_connectable`, `declarative_net_request`, `optional_permissions`; the failure message says a change needs docs/privacy.md and docs/decisions.md updates

An E2E test reads `chrome.permissions.getAll()` and `chrome.runtime.getManifest()` from the loaded extension and asserts the same allowlist, so the shipped build is checked, not only the manifest source

Settings gets a 'Privacy and permissions' group listing the live permissions (`chrome.permissions.getAll()`, updated on `permissions.onAdded/onRemoved`) in plain language, with the sentence 'Prowl cannot see or change the pages you visit: it has no access to your tabs or their content.' and a link to the privacy page; github.com is listed only while it is granted

docs/privacy.md, README, the site (landing + privacy page) and docs/chrome-web-store.md (permission justifications) state the guarantee with a permission table: what each permission allows, what Chrome's install prompt shows, and what Prowl can never do
Unit + component tests; E2E for the settings group with axe clean in light and dark; settings screenshot regenerated
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)
userStories.notes: Lock in tests/fixtures/manifestLock.ts (unit, plus e2e on dist-e2e and dist), live Privacy and permissions group in Settings, permission tables in privacy.md, README, site and store doc; 96 e2e, settings.png regenerated.

userStories.title: Section navigation as a bottom bar
userStories.description: As a user I want the section menu at the bottom of the panel, always reachable, with every section visible at a glance.
acceptanceCriteria: Section tabs move from the top to a bottom navigation bar fixed under the scrolling list; the header (logo, updated time, refresh, settings, account) and the quick filter stay on top; the bar shows only in the list view and is hidden when a single section is enabled (as today)

Each item: an Octicons icon (authored: git-pull-request, review requested: eye, mentioned: mention, assigned: person, custom: filter; add paths to components/icons), a short label (Mine, Review, Mentions, Assigned; a custom section shows its label truncated with the full label as accessible name) and its count; the selected item is marked by more than color (indicator + weight) and exposed to assistive tech

No horizontal scroll from 320 to 600 px panel widths: at most 4 items plus a 'More' item opening the existing Menu with the remaining sections and their counts; 'More' shows as selected when the current section is in it
Keyboard: the existing tab keyboard model (arrows, Home/End) and the shortcuts in Shortcuts.tsx keep working; focus is visible; toasts and menus never cover the bar or get covered by it

Every E2E and unit test that used the top tabs is updated, docs/design.md describes the bar; axe clean in light and dark; `pnpm screenshots` regenerated and the PNGs inspected (alignment, truncation, dark mode)
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Hide PRs with no recent commit
userStories.description: As a user I want PRs whose last commit is older than N days (default 20) out of my way, without losing their notifications.
acceptanceCriteria: `PullRequest.lastCommitAt` (ISO) comes from the head commit's `committedDate` in the list query; mapper, tests/fixtures builders, model.ts docs and docs/architecture.md updated
Setting `hideStaleAfterDays` (integer 0-365, default 20, 0 = never hide) validated by normalizeSettings and editable in Settings as 'Hide PRs with no commit for N days' with help text
A pure helper in src/lib decides whether a PR is hidden (`now` injected); it applies to every section (presets, custom, later team sections)

Hidden PRs are left out of the list, the section counts and the badge (`computeBadge` gets the setting); a 'Show N hidden' button at the end of the section reveals them for the session, each revealed card saying 'No commit for N d'; 'Hide again' collapses them
Notifications are unchanged: hidden PRs are still fetched and still notify (docs/decisions.md says so, and why committedDate)
Unit tests (mapper, helper, settings, badge, list model) and E2E (hidden by default, reveal, setting change applies live, 0 disables); screenshot regenerated if the list changed
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Hide drafts and bot PRs
userStories.description: As a user I want to hide draft PRs and PRs opened by bots (Dependabot, Renovate...) with one switch each.
acceptanceCriteria: `Actor.isBot`: true when GraphQL `author.__typename` is `Bot` or the login ends with `[bot]`; mapper, fixtures and model.ts updated
Settings `hideDrafts` and `hideBots` (both default false) with toggles in Settings

They extend US-034's hidden-PR helper: out of the list, counts and badge, revealed by the same single 'Show N hidden' button; revealed cards say why (Draft, Bot, No commit for N d); notifications unchanged
Unit tests and E2E (each toggle, combined reasons, reveal); axe clean
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Group PRs by repository
userStories.description: As a user I want to see the PRs of a section grouped by repository.
acceptanceCriteria: Setting `groupByRepo` (default false), independent of `sort`, toggled in Settings

When on, each section is grouped under repository headers (`owner/name`, count); groups are ordered by their first PR under the current sort (alphabetically when sort = repo) and PRs inside a group follow the sort

Headers are collapsible buttons (aria-expanded, keyboard operable, labelled with repo and count); collapsed state lasts for the session; the quick filter, the 'Show N hidden' reveal, seen marking and keyboard card navigation all work with groups (collapsed groups are skipped)
Pure grouping in the list model with unit tests; component tests; E2E; axe clean in light and dark; screenshot docs/screenshots/list-grouped.png
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Team review requests: discovery and fetching
userStories.description: As a member of GitHub teams I want a section with the PRs whose review is requested from my teams, discovered automatically.
acceptanceCriteria: Device flow requests `repo read:org`; the PAT link asks for `repo,read:org`; validatePat warns (does not fail) without read:org: team review requests need it; docs/auth.md explains read:org (classic/OAuth) and organization permission Members: read (fine-grained)

`fetchViewerTeams(client)` uses REST `GET /user/teams` (paginated, capped with a decisions.md entry) -> `{ org, slug, name }[]`; stored under a new storage key with `fetchedAt` and an error kind (missing scope, forbidden...), fetched at sign-in or when absent and refreshed by the poller at most every 24 h; a panel message can force a refresh

New built-in section kind `team_review_requested` (label 'Team reviews'): one search per followed team `is:pr is:open team-review-requested:<org>/<slug> archived:false` + repo filters, merged, de-duplicated, sorted by update and capped at maxPerSection; setting `unfollowedTeams` (default empty = follow every discovered team, new teams followed automatically)
The `review_requested` preset becomes direct requests only (`user-review-requested:@me`); docs explain team requests now live in 'Team reviews'

`Snapshot.teamRequests` (PR id -> team keys whose search returned it) for the cards; a missing scope, no team or a refused team search sets the team section's `sectionErrors` entry with an actionable message and never fails the whole poll
Mock GitHub server answers `GET /user/teams`; unit tests keep src/lib/github >= 95% coverage; docs/architecture.md (model, storage, data flow) and docs/decisions.md updated
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.description: As a member of GitHub teams I want to choose which teams to follow and see on each card which of my teams was asked to review.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings 'Teams' group: discovered teams grouped by organization with checkboxes (follow/unfollow, refetches), 'Refresh teams', last refresh time, and the missing-scope state explaining read:org / Members: read with a 'Sign in again' action

Cards whose PR has `snapshot.teamRequests` show 'Review requested from @org/team' (part of the card's accessible name); the expanded details list requested teams among reviewers
Onboarding copy and the PAT instructions mention read:org
Component tests; E2E (teams discovered, follow/unfollow, team chips, missing scope); axe clean; screenshots regenerated and inspected
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Update branch and auto-merge
userStories.description: As a PR author I want to update a branch that is behind and turn auto-merge on or off from the panel.
acceptanceCriteria: Model: `autoMerge: { method: MergeMethod; enabledBy: string | null } | null` and `autoMergeAllowed` (repository setting) mapped from the list query; fixtures updated

Actions in src/lib/github/actions.ts: update branch (`updatePullRequestBranch` with `expectedHeadOid`, merge or rebase), enable auto-merge (`enablePullRequestAutoMerge` with a method) and disable it (`disablePullRequestAutoMerge`); operations named Prowl*

Details Actions row via runPrAction: 'Update branch' (merge / rebase choice) when the PR is behind and the viewer can update; 'Enable auto-merge' (method picker reusing the merge dialog's) when the repo allows it, the PR is not yet mergeable and the viewer can merge; 'Disable auto-merge' when on; the card shows an 'Auto-merge' chip (not color-only)
Unit tests (mapper, actions), component tests, E2E with mock mutations; axe clean
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Keyboard shortcut to open the panel and notification buttons
userStories.description: As a user I want to open Prowl from the keyboard and act on a notification directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Manifest `commands` opens the side panel with a suggested shortcut (Alt+Shift+P; check conflicts and the current docs with Context7): `_execute_action` with openPanelOnActionClick if that opens the panel, else a named command calling `chrome.sidePanel.open` from `commands.onCommand` registered synchronously in register.ts; the US-032 manifest test allows the `commands` key (no new permission)
Settings shows the current shortcut (`chrome.commands.getAll`) and how to change it at chrome://extensions/shortcuts (as text)

Single-PR notifications get two buttons, 'Open' and 'Snooze 1 h' (`buttons` + `notifications.onButtonClicked` registered at startup); snooze goes through updatePrLocal and clears the notification; summary notifications get none
The chrome fake gains commands and onButtonClicked; unit tests; E2E where Chrome allows (manifest commands, handler via the worker); README and docs/architecture.md updated
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

userStories.title: Sync settings across devices
userStories.description: As a user of Chrome on several computers I want my Prowl settings to follow me, never my token.
acceptanceCriteria: Opt-in switch 'Sync settings with your Chrome profile' (default off) in Settings with a note that settings go through Chrome sync and that the token and local PR state never do; the switch itself is device-local

When on, settings are mirrored to `chrome.storage.sync` (one key, within QUOTA_BYTES_PER_ITEM; an over-quota or failed write shows an error and keeps local settings) and changes from other devices are applied through normalizeSettings (untrusted input) with last-write-wins; turning it on adopts the newer of the local and synced copies

Only settings ever reach storage.sync: a unit test asserts auth, snapshot, pollState, prLocal and teams are never written there; listeners are registered synchronously in the worker; the chrome fake gains a `sync` area
Unit tests; E2E (turn on, a simulated sync change from the worker updates the open panel, turn off stops mirroring); docs/privacy.md and docs/architecture.md updated
`pnpm verify` passes (lint, types, coverage gates, build, size budget, E2E)

Site Lighthouse >= 95 in every category
